title: Trace one AutoGen run across its real boundaries
description: Compare execution models, advance one transition at a time, and inject failures to see where messages, state, and recovery responsibility live.

topologies.label: AgentChat single agent
topologies.detail: Application code owns one AssistantAgent and its bounded model/tool loop.

steps.detail: The application constructs the task and chooses which tools this invocation may expose.
The model can propose content or a tool call; it does not receive application authority.
The adapter checks trusted identity, ownership, approval, and idempotency before execution.
The result is bounded and validated before it becomes model-visible context.
The application checks the final contract and records a completed, blocked, or incomplete disposition.

topologies.label: Round-robin team
topologies.detail: Participants share the thread and take turns in a fixed order.

steps.detail: The application starts a run with limits, identity, telemetry context, and a termination policy.
The manager selects the next participant by order; the planner response is shared with the team.
Every participant in the team can receive the group thread, so disclosure scope must be deliberate.
AgentChat executes the tool within the agent; the team manager is not an authorization service.
The reviewer sees the trajectory and emits a response; extra turns consume latency and context.
The condition evaluates the response delta and the application validates the resulting disposition.

topologies.label: Core direct message
topologies.detail: A runtime-managed agent sends one addressed request and awaits the handler response.

steps.detail: The runtime receives factories and creates an agent instance when its AgentId first receives a message.
The sender awaits one receiver and can use the returned value as a response.
A handler exception propagates to the awaiting sender instead of becoming a successful response.
Runtime delivery does not replace authorization, timeout, or duplicate-effect controls.
The caller receives either the handler value or a propagated exception and chooses the next transition.

topologies.label: Core topic broadcast
topologies.detail: A publisher emits a one-way message to all matching subscriptions.

steps.detail: Topic and agent types determine which runtime-managed subscribers receive the message.
Publication returns no subscriber response, even if a handler returns a value.
A subscriber exception is logged and is not propagated back to the publisher.
Each subscriber needs its own authorization, deduplication, and observability contract.
The publisher cannot infer fan-out success, so subscriber health must be measured separately.

failures.label: No injected failure
failures.detail: Observe the normal message path and ownership changes.
failures.controlledResult: The run reaches its declared completion boundary.
failures.uncontrolledResult: The run reaches its declared completion boundary.

failures.label: Tool write times out
failures.detail: The external system may have committed even though no response arrived.
failures.controlledResult: Reconcile by idempotency key, then reuse the recorded result or retry safely.
failures.uncontrolledResult: Stop as an ambiguous effect; an automatic retry could duplicate the write.

failures.label: Runtime restarts
failures.detail: The process stops after a completed transition but before the run finishes.
failures.controlledResult: Load the last compatible quiescent checkpoint and reconcile in-flight effects.
failures.uncontrolledResult: Conversation and routing state are unavailable; restart only as a new run.

failures.label: Agent handler raises
failures.detail: Compare awaited direct delivery with one-way topic fan-out.
failures.controlledResult: Delivery semantics determine who observes the error; telemetry still records the failed handler.
failures.uncontrolledResult: Without a monitored error path, the caller or publisher can misclassify the run.
